note: Questions from the CBSE Class X Science board exam 2024, Q.P. code 31/1/1, published by CBSE at cbse.gov.in. Questions that need a figure or a drawing are left out (Q14, Q25(B), Q31, Q35(B)), and so is Q10, whose options are open to dispute. Solutions are written for this portal and are not CBSE's official marking scheme.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: When 2 mL of sodium hydroxide solution is added to few pieces of granulated zinc in a test tube and then warmed, the reaction that occurs can be written in the form of a balanced chemical equation as :
questions.solution: Zinc reacts with sodium hydroxide to form sodium zincate and hydrogen gas: 2NaOH + Zn → Na₂ZnO₂ + H₂. This is the only balanced option with the right products.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Select from the following a decomposition reaction in which source of energy for decomposition is light :
questions.solution: Silver bromide decomposes in sunlight (used in black and white photography). The FeSO₄ and CaCO₃ reactions need heat and the electrolysis of water needs electricity.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: A metal and a non-metal that exists in liquid state at the room temperature are respectively :
questions.solution: Mercury is the metal that is liquid at room temperature and bromine is the liquid non-metal.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Carbon compounds :
(i) are good conductors of electricity.
(ii) are bad conductors of electricity.
(iii) have strong forces of attraction between their molecules.
(iv) have weak forces of attraction between their molecules.
The correct statements are :
questions.solution: Carbon compounds are covalent: they do not form ions, so they conduct electricity poorly, and the forces between their molecules are weak (hence low melting and boiling points).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Consider the following compounds : FeSO₄ ; CuSO₄ ; CaSO₄ ; Na₂CO₃
The compound having maximum number of water of crystallisation in its crystalline form in one molecule is :
questions.solution: FeSO₄·7H₂O, CuSO₄·5H₂O, CaSO₄·2H₂O and Na₂CO₃·10H₂O. Washing soda has the most, 10 molecules.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Oxides of aluminium and zinc are :
questions.solution: Al₂O₃ and ZnO react with both acids and bases to give salt and water, so they are amphoteric.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
MnO₂ + 4HCl → MnCl₂ + 2H₂O + Cl₂
The reaction given above is a redox reaction because in this case :
options: MnO₂ is oxidised and HCl is reduced.
MnO₂ is reduced and HCl is oxidised.
questions.solution: MnO₂ loses oxygen (reduced) and HCl loses hydrogen to form Cl₂ (oxidised). Both happen together, which makes it a redox reaction.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Consider the following statements :
(i) The sex of a child is determined by what it inherits from the mother.
(ii) The sex of a child is determined by what it inherits from the father.
(iii) The probability of having a male child is more than that of a female child.
(iv) The sex of a child is determined at the time of fertilisation when male and female gametes fuse to form a zygote.
The correct statements are :
questions.solution: The mother always gives an X chromosome; the father gives X or Y, so the father's contribution decides the sex, at fertilisation. Boys and girls are equally likely.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Chromosomes :
(i) carry hereditary information from parents to the next generation.
(ii) are thread like structures located inside the nucleus of an animal cell.
(iii) always exist in pairs in human reproductive cells.
(iv) are involved in the process of cell division.
The correct statements are :
questions.solution: Statements (i), (ii) and (iv) are true. (iii) is false: reproductive cells (gametes) have only one chromosome of each pair.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
A stomata closes when :
(i) it needs carbon dioxide for photosynthesis.
(ii) it does not need carbon dioxide for photosynthesis.
(iii) water flows out of the guard cells.
(iv) water flows into the guard cells.
The correct reason(s) in this process is/are :
questions.solution: Stomata close when CO₂ is not needed for photosynthesis; the guard cells lose water, shrink and close the pore.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: At what distance from a convex lens should an object be placed to get an image of the same size as that of the object on a screen ?
options: Beyond twice the focal length of the lens.
At the principal focus of the lens.
At twice the focal length of the lens.
Between the optical centre of the lens and its principal focus.
questions.solution: An object at 2F₁ gives a real, inverted image of the same size at 2F₂.

questions.subject: Science
questions.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.text: The lens system of human eye forms an image on a light sensitive screen, which is called as :
questions.solution: The image is formed on the retina, the light-sensitive screen at the back of the eye.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Identify the food chain in which the organisms of the second trophic level are missing :
options: Zooplankton, Phytoplankton, small fish, large fish
questions.solution: The second trophic level is the herbivores. 'Tiger, grass, snake, frog' has a producer and carnivores but no herbivore (such as a grasshopper or deer).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: In which of the following organisms, multiple fission is a means of asexual reproduction ?
questions.solution: Plasmodium (the malaria parasite) divides into many daughter cells at once by multiple fission. Leishmania and Paramoecium use binary fission and yeast reproduces by budding.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Assertion (A): Hydrogen gas is not evolved when zinc reacts with nitric acid.
Reason (R): Nitric acid oxidises the hydrogen gas produced to water and itself gets reduced.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: Nitric acid is a strong oxidising agent: it oxidises the hydrogen formed to water and is itself reduced to nitrogen oxides. That is exactly why no hydrogen gas is evolved.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Assertion (A): Accumulation of harmful chemicals is maximum in the organisms at the highest trophic level of a food chain.
Reason (R): Harmful chemicals are sprayed on the crops to protect them from diseases and pests.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: Non-biodegradable chemicals build up at each step of the food chain (biological magnification), so A is true. R is true, but spraying crops does not explain why the concentration is highest at the top.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Assertion (A): The rate of breathing in aquatic organisms is much faster than in terrestrial organisms.
Reason (R): The amount of oxygen dissolved in water is very high as compared to the amount of oxygen in air.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: Aquatic animals do breathe faster, so A is true. The reason is that water holds much less dissolved oxygen than air contains, so R is false.

questions.subject: Science
questions.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.text:
Assertion (A): The rainbow is a natural spectrum of sunlight in the sky.
Reason (R): Rainbow is formed in the sky when the sun is overhead and water droplets are also present in air.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: A rainbow is a natural spectrum caused by dispersion of sunlight in raindrops, so A is true. It is seen with the sun behind the observer (low in the sky), not overhead, so R is false.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Name the type of chemical reaction in which calcium oxide reacts with water. Justify your answer by giving balanced chemical equation for the chemical reaction.
questions.solution: It is a combination reaction (and also exothermic): two substances combine to form a single product, slaked lime. CaO(s) + H₂O(l) → Ca(OH)₂(aq) + heat.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: State one role of each of the following in human digestive system : (i) Hydrochloric acid (ii) Villi (iii) Anal Sphincter (iv) Lipase
questions.solution: (i) Hydrochloric acid makes the stomach acidic so that pepsin can act, and kills germs in food. (ii) Villi increase the surface area of the small intestine for absorbing digested food. (iii) The anal sphincter controls the exit of faeces from the body. (iv) Lipase breaks down (emulsified) fats into fatty acids and glycerol.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: How is the movement of leaves of a sensitive plant different from the downward movement of the roots ?
questions.solution: Leaves of the sensitive plant fold quickly in response to touch; this movement is not related to growth and does not depend on the direction of the stimulus. Roots grow downward slowly in response to gravity (positive geotropism); this is a growth movement directed by the stimulus.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: There is a hormone which regulates carbohydrate, protein and fat metabolism in our body. Name the hormone and the gland which secretes it. Why is it important for us to have iodised salt in our diet?
questions.solution: The hormone is thyroxine, secreted by the thyroid gland. Iodine is needed by the thyroid to make thyroxine; lack of iodine can cause goitre (a swollen neck), so iodised salt is recommended.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: An object is placed at a distance of 10 cm from a convex mirror of focal length 15 cm. Find the position of the image formed by the mirror.
questions.solution: u = −10 cm, f = +15 cm. 1/v + 1/u = 1/f gives 1/v = 1/15 + 1/10 = 5/30 = 1/6, so v = +6 cm. The image is 6 cm behind the mirror (virtual, erect and diminished).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Show how you would connect three resistors each of resistance 6 Ω, so that the combination has a resistance of 9 Ω. Also justify your answer.
questions.solution: Connect two of the resistors in parallel and the third in series with that pair. The parallel pair gives 1/R = 1/6 + 1/6, so R = 3 Ω; adding 6 Ω in series gives 3 + 6 = 9 Ω.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(i) Two magnetic field lines do not intersect each other. Why ?
(ii) How is a uniform magnetic field in a given region represented ? Draw a diagram in support of your answer.
questions.solution: (i) If two field lines crossed, a compass needle at that point would have to point in two directions at once, which is impossible. (ii) A uniform field is shown by parallel straight lines that are equally spaced (as inside a long solenoid); the diagram shows such lines with arrows in one direction.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Write one chemical equation each for the chemical reaction in which the following have taken place : (i) Change in colour (ii) Change in temperature (iii) Formation of precipitate. Mention colour change/temperature change (rise/fall)/compound precipitated along with equation.
questions.solution: (i) Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu: the blue copper sulphate solution turns pale green. (ii) CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ + heat: the temperature rises. (iii) Na₂SO₄ + BaCl₂ → BaSO₄ + 2NaCl: a white precipitate of barium sulphate forms. (Other correct examples are accepted.)

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(i) The pH of a sample of tomato juice is 4.6. How is this juice likely to be in taste ? Give reason to justify your answer.
(ii) How do we differentiate between a strong acid and a weak base in terms of ion-formation in aqueous solutions ?
(iii) The acid rain can make the survival of aquatic animals difficult. How ?
questions.solution: (i) Sour, because a pH below 7 means the juice is acidic. (ii) A strong acid ionises almost completely in water, giving a large number of H⁺ ions; a weak base ionises only partly, giving few OH⁻ ions. (iii) Acid rain lowers the pH of rivers and lakes. Aquatic animals survive only in a narrow pH range (about 7 to 7.8), so the more acidic water harms them.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(i) Why is respiratory pigment needed in multicellular organisms with large body size ?
(ii) Give reasons for the following : (a) Rings of cartilage are present in the throat. (b) Lungs always contain a residual volume of air. (c) The diaphragm flattens and ribs are lifted up when we breathe in. (d) Walls of alveoli contain an extensive network of blood vessels.
questions.solution: (i) In a large body, diffusion alone is too slow to supply oxygen to all cells, so a pigment such as haemoglobin, which has a high affinity for oxygen, carries it from the lungs to the tissues. (ii) (a) They stop the air passage from collapsing. (b) So there is enough time for oxygen to be absorbed and carbon dioxide released. (c) This enlarges the chest cavity, so air is drawn into the lungs. (d) For the exchange of gases between the air in the alveoli and the blood.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Define reflex action. With the help of a flow chart show the path of a reflex action such as sneezing.
questions.solution: A reflex action is a sudden, automatic (involuntary) response to a stimulus, carried out without conscious thinking. Sneezing: stimulus (irritant in the nose) → receptors in the nose → sensory neuron → medulla in the hindbrain (relay) → motor neuron → effector muscles of the chest and diaphragm → sneeze.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Name and state the rule to determine the direction of a : (i) magnetic field produced around a current carrying straight conductor. (ii) force experienced by a current carrying straight conductor placed in a magnetic field which is perpendicular to it.
questions.solution: (i) Right-hand thumb rule: hold the conductor in your right hand with the thumb pointing along the current; your curled fingers give the direction of the magnetic field lines. (ii) Fleming's left-hand rule: stretch the thumb, forefinger and middle finger of the left hand at right angles to each other. If the forefinger points along the field and the middle finger along the current, the thumb gives the direction of the force (motion).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Plants → Deer → Lion
In the given food chain, what will be the impact of removing all the organisms of second trophic level on the first and third trophic level? Will the impact be the same for the organisms of the third trophic level in the above food chain if they were present in a food web? Justify.
questions.solution: Without deer, plants (first level) would increase because nothing grazes on them, and lions (third level) would starve and decline. In a food web the impact on lions would be smaller, because they could feed on other herbivores instead.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: A gas 'X' which is a deadly poison is found at the higher levels of atmosphere and performs an essential function. Name the gas and write the function performed by this gas in the atmosphere. Which chemical is linked to the decrease in the level of this gas? What measures have been taken by an international organization to check the depletion of the layer containing this gas?
questions.solution: X is ozone (O₃). The ozone layer shields the Earth from harmful ultraviolet radiation from the sun. Its depletion is linked to chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) used in refrigerants and fire extinguishers. In 1987 the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) got countries to agree to freeze CFC production at 1986 levels and phase it out.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(i) Define a homologous series of carbon compounds.
(ii) Why is the melting and boiling points of C₄H₈ higher than that of C₃H₆ or C₂H₄ ?
(iii) Why do we NOT see any gradation in chemical properties of a homologous series compounds ?
(iv) Write the name and structures of (i) aldehyde and (ii) ketone with molecular form C₃H₆O.
questions.solution: (i) A series of carbon compounds with the same functional group and similar chemical properties, in which successive members differ by a –CH₂– unit (14 u). (ii) C₄H₈ has the highest molecular mass, and melting and boiling points rise with molecular mass in a series. (iii) Chemical properties are decided by the functional group, which is the same in every member. (iv) Aldehyde: propanal, CH₃–CH₂–CHO. Ketone: propanone (acetone), CH₃–CO–CH₃.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(i) Write the name and structure of an organic compound 'X' having two carbon atoms in its molecule and its name is suffixed with '–ol'.
(ii) What happens when 'X' is heated with excess concentrated sulphuric acid at 443 K? Write chemical equation for the reaction stating the conditions for the reaction. Also state the role played by concentrated sulphuric acid in the reaction.
(iii) Name and draw the electron dot structure of hydrocarbon produced in the above reaction.
questions.solution: (i) X is ethanol, CH₃–CH₂–OH. (ii) It is dehydrated to ethene: CH₃CH₂OH → CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O (heated with excess concentrated H₂SO₄ at 443 K). Concentrated sulphuric acid acts as a dehydrating agent, removing water. (iii) Ethene, C₂H₄: the two carbon atoms share two electron pairs (a double bond), and each carbon shares one pair with each of its two hydrogen atoms.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(i) Name three techniques/devices used by human females to avoid pregnancy. Mention the side effects caused by each.
(ii) What will happen if in a human female (a) fertilisation takes place, (b) an egg is not fertilised ?
questions.solution: (i) Oral contraceptive pills: change the hormone balance and can cause side effects such as nausea or hormonal imbalance. Copper-T (IUCD) placed in the uterus: can cause irritation of the uterus. Surgical blocking of the fallopian tubes (tubectomy): surgery carries a risk of infection and other problems if not done properly. (ii) (a) The zygote implants in the thickened wall of the uterus and develops into an embryo, nourished through the placenta. (b) The thick, spongy uterus lining is not needed; it breaks down and comes out through the vagina as blood and mucus (menstruation), roughly every month.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(i) Define electric power. Express it in terms of potential difference (V) and resistance (R).
(ii) An electric oven is designed to work on the mains voltage of 220 V. This oven consumes 11 units of electrical energy in 5 hours. Calculate : (a) power rating of the oven (b) current drawn by the oven (c) resistance of the oven when it is red hot
questions.solution: (i) Electric power is the rate at which electrical energy is consumed: P = V²/R. (ii) (a) P = 11 kWh ÷ 5 h = 2.2 kW = 2200 W. (b) I = P/V = 2200 ÷ 220 = 10 A. (c) R = V/I = 220 ÷ 10 = 22 Ω.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
(i) Write the relation between resistance R and electrical resistivity ρ of the material of a conductor in the shape of cylinder of length l and area of cross-section A. Hence derive the SI unit of electrical resistivity.
(ii) The resistance of a metal wire of length 3 m is 60 Ω. If the area of cross-section of the wire is 4 × 10⁻⁷ m², calculate the electrical resistivity of the wire.
(iii) State how would electrical resistivity be affected if the wire (of part 'ii') is stretched so that its length is doubled. Justify your answer.
questions.solution: (i) R = ρl/A, so ρ = RA/l, with unit Ω × m²/m = Ω m. (ii) ρ = (60 × 4 × 10⁻⁷)/3 = 8 × 10⁻⁶ Ω m. (iii) Resistivity does not change: it depends only on the material (and temperature), not on the length or thickness. (The resistance becomes four times larger.)

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
The metals produced by various reduction processes are not very pure. They contain impurities, which must be removed to obtain pure metals. The most widely used method for refining impure metals is electrolytic refining.

What is the cathode and anode made of in the refining of copper by this process ?
questions.solution: The cathode is a thin strip of pure copper and the anode is the impure copper.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
The metals produced by various reduction processes are not very pure. They contain impurities, which must be removed to obtain pure metals. The most widely used method for refining impure metals is electrolytic refining.

Name the solution used in the above process and write its formula.
questions.solution: Acidified copper sulphate solution, CuSO₄.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
The metals produced by various reduction processes are not very pure. They contain impurities, which must be removed to obtain pure metals. The most widely used method for refining impure metals is electrolytic refining.

How copper gets refined when electric current is passed in the electrolytic cell ?
questions.solution: Copper from the impure anode dissolves into the solution as Cu²⁺ ions (Cu → Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻). An equal amount of pure copper from the solution is deposited on the cathode (Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu). Soluble impurities stay in the solution and insoluble ones settle below the anode as anode mud.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
The metals produced by various reduction processes are not very pure. They contain impurities, which must be removed to obtain pure metals.

You have two beakers 'A' and 'B' containing copper sulphate solution. What would you observe after about 2 hours if you dip a strip of zinc in beaker 'A' and a strip of silver in beaker 'B'? Give reason for your observations in each case.
questions.solution: Beaker A: the blue colour fades and a reddish-brown layer of copper forms on the zinc, because zinc is more reactive than copper and displaces it (Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu). Beaker B: no change, because silver is less reactive than copper and cannot displace it.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Mendel worked out the rules of heredity by working on garden pea using a number of visible contrasting characters. He conducted several experiments by making a cross with one or two pairs of contrasting characters of pea plant. On the basis of his observations he gave some interpretations which helped to study the mechanism of inheritance.

When Mendel crossed pea plants with pure tall and pure short characteristics to produce F₁ progeny, which two observations were made by him in F₁ plants?
questions.solution: All the F₁ plants were tall, and there were no plants of medium (in-between) height; only one of the two parental traits was seen.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Mendel worked out the rules of heredity by working on garden pea using a number of visible contrasting characters. On the basis of his observations he gave some interpretations which helped to study the mechanism of inheritance.

Write one difference between dominant and recessive trait.
questions.solution: A dominant trait shows up even when only one copy of its gene is present (for example Tt is tall); a recessive trait shows up only when both copies are recessive (tt).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Mendel worked out the rules of heredity by working on garden pea using a number of visible contrasting characters.

In a cross with two pairs of contrasting characters RRYY (Round Yellow) × rryy (Wrinkled Green), Mendel observed 4 types of combinations in F₂ generation. By which method did he obtain F₂ generation ? Write the ratio of the parental combinations obtained and what conclusions were drawn from this experiment.
questions.solution: He obtained F₂ by self-pollinating the F₁ plants (RrYy). F₂ ratio: 9 round yellow : 3 round green : 3 wrinkled yellow : 1 wrinkled green, so the parental combinations appear in the ratio 9 : 1. Conclusion: the two traits (seed shape and seed colour) are inherited independently of each other, which is why new combinations appear.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Mendel worked out the rules of heredity by working on garden pea using a number of visible contrasting characters.

Justify the statement : "It is possible that a trait is inherited but may not be expressed."
questions.solution: When pure tall (TT) and pure short (tt) plants are crossed, all F₁ plants (Tt) are tall: they carry the gene for shortness but do not show it. When the F₁ plants are self-pollinated, about a quarter of the F₂ plants are short, showing that the short trait was inherited all along but not expressed because it is recessive.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Study the data given below showing the focal length of three concave mirrors A, B and C and the respective distances of objects placed in front of the mirrors :

Case 1 : Mirror A : focal length 20 cm : object distance 45 cm
Case 2 : Mirror B : focal length 15 cm : object distance 30 cm
Case 3 : Mirror C : focal length 30 cm : object distance 20 cm

In which one of the above cases the mirror will form a diminished image of the object ? Justify your answer.
questions.solution: Case 1. The object (45 cm) is beyond the centre of curvature (2f = 40 cm), so the image forms between F and C and is diminished.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Study the data given below showing the focal length of three concave mirrors A, B and C and the respective distances of objects placed in front of the mirrors :

Case 1 : Mirror A : focal length 20 cm : object distance 45 cm
Case 2 : Mirror B : focal length 15 cm : object distance 30 cm
Case 3 : Mirror C : focal length 30 cm : object distance 20 cm

List two properties of the image formed in case 2.
questions.solution: The object is at the centre of curvature (30 cm = 2f), so the image is real and inverted, and the same size as the object (formed at C).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text:
Study the data given below showing the focal length of three concave mirrors A, B and C and the respective distances of objects placed in front of the mirrors :

Case 1 : Mirror A : focal length 20 cm : object distance 45 cm
Case 2 : Mirror B : focal length 15 cm : object distance 30 cm
Case 3 : Mirror C : focal length 30 cm : object distance 20 cm

What is the nature and size of the image formed by mirror C ? Draw ray diagram to justify your answer.
questions.solution: The object (20 cm) is between the pole and the focus (30 cm), so the image is virtual, erect and magnified, formed behind the mirror. Ray diagram: a ray parallel to the axis reflects through F, and a ray through C (or towards the pole) reflects back; the reflected rays diverge and appear to meet behind the mirror.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: An object is placed at a distance of 18 cm from the pole of a concave mirror of focal length 12 cm. Find the position of the image formed in this case.
questions.solution: u = −18 cm, f = −12 cm. 1/v = 1/f − 1/u = −1/12 + 1/18 = (−3 + 2)/36 = −1/36, so v = −36 cm. The image is 36 cm in front of the mirror (real, inverted and magnified).
